title: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
body:
Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03219

Recently, harness self-evolution has emerged as an important paradigm for improving agent performance. Prior studies show that evolving the agent harness can effectively enhance agent capabilities without modifying the foundation model's parameters. We find that existing approaches largely study agent evolution on a single task. In practice, coding agents may need to handle multiple task types over time. Whether an agent harness can continuously evolve across multiple tasks without suffering from catastrophic forgetting remains an important open question.
  In this paper, we investigate this open question through a comprehensive empirical study of continual harness self-evolution. We organize three software engineering task datasets into six different evolution directions and apply two representative harness evolution methods to perform continual evolution along these directions. Our experimental results show that evolution on a subsequent dataset can substantially undermine the performance on previously seen datasets. For example, with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, Meta-Harness improves its performance on SWE-Bench to 94.0% after evolution. However, after further evolution on FeatureBench, its performance on SWE-Bench drops to 32.0% by the fifth round, corresponding to a 66% relative decrease. Finally, based on our experimental findings, we identify several insights, providing directions for the continual self-evolution of agent harnesses. Code is available at https://github.com/THU-Agent/continual-harness-evolution.

title: EvoGroup: A Self-Evolving Harness for Group Agents in Shared Contexts
body:
EvoGroup: A Self-Evolving Harness for Group Agents in Shared Contexts

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03868

With the rise of Group Agent such as Claude Tag, agents increasingly serve as digital workers for long-term team collaboration. These agents operate over shared contexts that continuously accumulate through multi-user interactions. However, existing agent memory systems are mainly designed for individual users and struggle to capture group-level knowledge in shared contexts, including group relationships and collaboratively formed knowledge. Manual memory strategies further limit adaptation to diverse and evolving shared contexts. To this end, we propose \textbf{EvoGroup (EvoG)}, a self-evolving harness for group agents that starts from a minimal six-tool cold start and adapts through interaction with shared context. EvoG uses confidence and task outcomes to select informative trajectories, while also eliciting self-reflections on uncertainty in low-confidence cases. The analysis agent then examines selected trajectories through adaptive progressive disclosure, followed by bucketed analysis to synthesize high-level findings that guide the evolve agent in revising the Harness. Empirically, pass@1 on held-out split of EverMemBench improves from 71.07\% to 89.58\%, surpassing both self-evolving memory and human-designed harnesses, including Claude Code (85.83\%). To evaluate generalization, we freeze the evolved harness and evaluate it on the unseen GroupMemBench, where, with GPT-5.5, it demonstrates effective generalization and outperforms both memory baselines and human-designed harnesses.

title: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training
body:
Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04277

Harness evolution from a common base exhibits Locality, Complementarity, and Nonstationarity: variants repair different failures, and their utility changes as the policy learns. Rather than seeking a universally superior harness, we introduce Harness-S to selectively rescue failures of a base execution system through sibling harnesses and transfer the resulting capabilities into a single policy that remains effective under the original harness. Directional Harness Evolution develops specialized sibling harnesses along distinct repair directions, forming a reusable Sibling Harness Pool that remains fixed during policy training. Complementary Harness Rescue Training invokes this pool only when all initial attempts under the base harness fail. The same policy generates fresh rollouts under selected auxiliary harnesses, and these trajectories replace the failed group for reinforcement learning. An Adaptive Harness Router selects the Top-k variants using Harness Behavior Profiles and voting across multiple LLMs. Policy-aware profile re-anchoring refreshes this evidence as the policy learns. Across AppWorld, SWE-Gym, and DBBench, the trained policy substantially outperforms policy-only training when returned to the original base harness. Behavioral analyses and held-out cases support the transfer of harness-elicited behaviors into the policy itself. Reusing the router for Rank-1 inference provides additional gains at the same executor rollout count.

title: DualEvolve: Dual-Level Self-Evolution of Mechanism and Orchestration for Recommendation
body:
DualEvolve: Dual-Level Self-Evolution of Mechanism and Orchestration for Recommendation

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04439

Recommender systems are widely used in e-commerce and content platforms, where improvement requires repeated model design, training optimization, and experimental validation. Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate this development cycle. Sustained autonomous improvement requires agents to improve both recommendation models and their development workflows. However, task-performance-driven approaches select updates mainly by candidates' final scores, without a separate optimization signal for experimentation quality. We therefore present DualEvolve, a dual-level framework that co-evolves recommendation mechanisms and agent orchestration toward recursive self-improvement. Inner evolution revises model and training code using task feedback to improve recommendation performance. Outer evolution scores the inner-loop experimental process, updates harness and skill rules using these scores and execution traces, and adjusts orchestration choices based on next-round scores to improve the quality of subsequent experiments. Experiments on MovieLens-1M and three Amazon Reviews 2023 subsets cover four recommendation methods and 16 settings. DualEvolve achieves higher test means than Base, OpenEvolve, and DeepEvolve in all 64 setting-metric comparisons, with macro-averaged relative gains over DeepEvolve of 7.6% (HR@5) and 9.0% (NDCG@5).

title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
body:
Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05139

Harness optimization improves long-horizon agents by refining the prompts, tools, memory, and hooks around a frozen model. Offline methods can learn from completed trajectories, but deploy one shared harness that may overfit training tasks and cannot react to evidence revealed during a new run. Online evolution can adapt before, during, or after one run through an evolver, but may have to reason about every intervention from scratch or rely on verifier feedback that is usually unavailable at test time. We introduce Meta$^2$, which moves offline optimization one level up: rather than optimizing a shared harness, it learns reusable knowledge for harness evolution and applies it within each task online. Offline, Meta$^2$ learns a textual Meta-Skill $M$ by contrasting training rollouts of the same task agent under three configurations: without an evolver, with an evolver guided by the current version of $M$, and with an evolver given privileged verifier information available only in training. Contrasts in trajectories and outcomes are aggregated across tasks to refine $M$ into reusable guidance on when and how to evolve, when to leave the harness unchanged, and which interventions to avoid. Online, an evolver combines the frozen $M$ with emerging trajectory evidence to decide whether to KEEP the harness unchanged or EVOLVE it through a task-local edit. Each edit applies to the rest of the same run without resetting its environment or progress. Thus, evolution guidance transfers across tasks while harness edits remain task-local, and held-out verifier feedback is never available to the evolver. On two long-horizon benchmarks, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE 1.1, Meta$^2$ achieves the highest performance among evaluated methods with GPT-5.6-Terra, reaching 81.00% and 44.44%, respectively. Ablations support the value of contrastive evolution guidance and keeping online harness edits task-local.

title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
body:
Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06049

Personal agents draw on past conversations to tailor their responses to each user. Their memory systems store and update what each user says, and coding agents now also rewrite the harness that turns this memory into the model's context. Such patches risk overfitting, because one tested only on the failures it targets can fix those cases and help nowhere else. We present Reglos, a training-free personal memory agent that tests whether harness changes help beyond the failures they were written to fix. Its self-evolving memory adds to each user's append-only record with every conversation, as new preferences supersede old ones and facts can be forgotten. Its harness improves through recursive self-improvement, in which a coding agent proposes patches from failure traces and a critic from a second model family screens each one for benchmark gaming. After the harness is frozen, a fixed evaluator decides which further patches to accept. With the same backbone behind every system, Reglos outperforms state-of-the-art memory systems such as Mem0, MemOS and EverOS, reaching 61.3% and 84.0% on PersonaMem-v2 and LongMemEval-S with Qwen3.8-27B, and 57.5% and 87.2% with GPT-5.6 Luna.

title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
body:
HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06254

The performance of large language model (LLM) agents depends on both the underlying model and the harness that governs interaction with tools and the environment. Yet harness design remains largely manual, and automating it requires navigating an open-ended search space through costly end-to-end evaluations. We introduce HarnessFlow, a framework for optimizing complete executable harnesses under a limited candidate-evaluation budget, with the model and task environment held fixed. HarnessFlow organizes candidates and their evaluation histories in a refinement tree, using a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based policy to balance exploitation and exploration. A coding agent refines selected harnesses using archived code, execution feedback, and a library of reusable harness mechanisms. With 15 refinement attempts per benchmark, HarnessFlow achieves the highest mean test scores among the compared methods on six benchmarks spanning agentic tasks, coding, and web interaction. The optimized harnesses achieve an average score of 69.48%, outperforming the initial harnesses and Meta-Harness by 10.89 and 3.95 percentage points, respectively, while incurring lower average per-task execution costs than hand-engineered baselines. These results suggest that structured harness search offers a promising route toward automating the design of capable and efficient LLM agents.

title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World
body:
PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06768

Coding agents powered by models such as GPT-6-Astra connect spatial reasoning with executable robot behavior, raising the question of how such agents can produce lasting improvements in robot capabilities from physical interaction. In this work, we study embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) through real-world exploration, code refinement, and deployment using PyRUA-REAL, a framework in which coding agents retain interaction experience as persistent memory and reusable executable skills that inform subsequent exploration and improvement. Our empirical study places physical manipulation at the center of the improvement process, examining how agents collaborate, what kinds of execution feedback support effective code refinement, and how task specifications and previously acquired skills influence robustness and task transfer. We further investigate the efficiency and capability of the resulting programs when deployed without involving an online agent for decision-making. Across eight real-world tasks, PyRUA-REAL achieves an average success rate of 91.1%. In complementary evaluation on 42 tasks from the RoboDojo benchmark, it achieves an average success rate of 84.4%. This study provides empirical guidance for turning physical exploration into reusable robot skills that support continued improvement and robust, efficient deployment.

title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
body:
CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06858

Recursive self-improvement requires AI systems to improve the models and infrastructure used by subsequent systems. LLM compression offers a concrete efficiency objective: retain a pretrained model's behavior within a smaller model storage budget. We study whether coding agents can carry out this step autonomously. We formulate compression as a terminal task in which an agent receives a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget, then constructs compressed weights and executable inference code. The agent controls its algorithm and experiments; perplexity feedback guides search, and independent verification checks the final model. Across six agents and six model--size settings, 29 of 36 submissions pass verification. Selecting the lowest-perplexity agent design per task yields an average 3.4% perplexity increase over BF16 and 77.33% downstream accuracy, compared with 79.56% for BF16. Recorded experiments reveal how agents achieve these outcomes and where improvement breaks down. Agents lower PPL in 21 of 24 revisions at nearly fixed storage; complete-model feedback reverses 17 of 79 prior local rankings; and generation and inference tests expose failures that likelihood alone misses. The results identify representation design, experimental judgment, and capability validation as central to agent-driven model compression, a measurable component of efficiency-oriented self-improvement.

title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
body:
Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07048

Evolution has shaped intelligence for billions of years. Artificial intelligence (AI) now raises a striking possibility: intelligence may begin to direct its own evolution. As AI agents become capable of modifying and evaluating their own behavior, how quickly could they improve, and how can that improvement remain safe? We develop a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution following environmental change. Darwinian evolution relies on natural selection, Lamarckian evolution adds inherited learning, and agent-directed evolution allows agents to generate and evaluate behavioral variants and choose how extensively to search. When learning is sufficiently effective, these mechanisms exhibit progressively faster adaptation. Generating more variants accelerates adaptation, while optimal search effort depends on learning ability, problem difficulty, and experimentation costs. However, an agent's ability to direct its improvement does not ensure that improvements are evaluated against the intended objective. When the evaluation target is misspecified, additional search accelerates convergence toward the wrong behavior, even as measured performance improves. In recursive self-improvement, such errors may persist across generations, posing challenges for AI safety. Independent evaluation and oversight must keep pace with autonomous AI development. The central challenge is not simply to accelerate the evolution of intelligence, but to preserve humanity's ability to guide its direction, limit its speed, and intervene when necessary.

title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
body:
EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07372

An LLM agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company's Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets. We call these environments stationary environments. We introduce EnvOpt, a method for automated end-to-end optimization of stationary environments for any given model and harness, using real or synthetic tasks without needing any graders or reference answers. On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduces the cost of Claude Haiku 4.5 by 72.7% and raises its pass rate by 14.34%. The same environment transfers to Opus 5, cutting its cost by 68.1% with a 1.34% gain. Added on top of Meta-Harness's optimized harness for Haiku 4.5, it lowers cost by a further 83.4% and adds 11.17% accuracy over Meta-Harness alone. Across 5 benchmarks, EnvOpt significantly reduces the cost of agents while improving or maintaining pass rate, and is transferable to different models and different harnesses. We also discuss common successful and rejected environment optimization strategies during automated optimization. More broadly, our results show that how information is represented to an agent shapes both its cost and its success, making the environment worth optimizing in addition to the parameters and the harness.

title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
body:
Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07624

Agent harness evolution enables recursive self-improvement (RSI) without updating model weights. We examine whether higher benchmark scores yield reliable, efficient, and transferable improvement. We evaluate four methods across harnesses, general and coding tasks. Repeated evaluations, controlled agent expansion, component interventions, and admission replays reveal recurring patterns. All sixteen evolved agents gain previously uncovered tasks while losing previously covered ones. In one general-task case, reliability rises by 5.2 points despite losing ten previously covered tasks. Most reliability gains also increase deployment cost. Specific changes usually outperform generic reminders, but their benefits can change when combined. The highest-scoring agent does not yield the largest mean improvement in any of our four pools, and stricter admission can discard useful alternatives. Transfer selectively preserves gains: coverage usually falls on the general-task target across both harness types and paradigms, but rises on the coding target with the outer-layer-only harness. These findings motivate preservation-aware evaluation, tested decision rules, and explicit applicability conditions. As a constructive follow-up, EvoAudit turns these diagnostics into revisions of select, analyze, mutate, and gate, achieving the best performance.

title: Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents
body:
Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08946

Frontier language models are increasingly deployed as agents, and how well an agent performs depends not only on its model but also on its harness: the prompts, tools, memory, and control loop through which the model acts. When an agent is applied to a new problem, a natural question is whether it can use the feedback of the task to improve the way it works, and not merely its answer. Most existing benchmarks keep the agent's harness fixed and score the solution it produces, or target large-scale model training. We introduce Flex-RSI, a benchmark for the recursive self-improvement of agents on vision and robotics tasks under a fixed budget. In each round, an executor improves the task solution, which is kept only if it scores higher on held-out validation data, and an improver then revises the harness, including the executor and itself. Every run starts from the same general-purpose harness, and the final solution is scored on hidden test data. Evaluating closed-source and open-weight models on tasks spanning perception, reasoning, robot action, 3D reconstruction, visual creation, and infrastructure, we find that self-improvement helps most when the agent builds its own solution, that feedback recording only success or failure holds back open-weight models, and that open-weight models fall furthest behind where outputs must pass strict checks of physical stability or exact correctness. Paired runs further show that editing the harness itself contributes to the gains.

title: BOXBOX: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Running Performance Optimization
body:
BOXBOX: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Running Performance Optimization

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09218

Automated harness optimization improves agents by learning from trajectories and task feedback. Existing offline methods use reference answers to optimize harnesses for reuse on held-out tasks. However, many real-world tasks are open-ended, while long runs expose new difficulties that offline-optimized harnesses may not address. To study harness optimization in these settings, we introduce PerfRace, a benchmark for long-running performance optimization of software projects, and investigate whether agents can use task-specific experience to recursively improve their harnesses during an ongoing task. To this end, we introduce BOXBOX, which enables agent-triggered harness revision and kernel-managed hot reloading while preserving execution context. We evaluate BOXBOX on PerfRace under matched test-time budgets, comparing it with Frozen Harness, offline Harness Evolution, and Harness Scaling. BOXBOX achieves higher speedup with more efficient use of task time and model cost, reaching a Speedup@4h of 1.70x, compared with 1.54x for the strongest baseline.

title: Recursively Self-Improving Electromagnetic Spectrum Agents: Architecture and Operation
body:
Recursively Self-Improving Electromagnetic Spectrum Agents: Architecture and Operation

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09318

Electromagnetic spectrum agents (ESAs) must contend with changing environments and task requirements during sustained autonomous operation, yet their existing capabilities may not remain suitable for new operating conditions. This article proposes recursively self-improving electromagnetic spectrum agents (RSI-ESAs) that use operational feedback to update their capabilities and build on prior improvements. We present their architecture and editable components, and describe a self-improvement process encompassing problem diagnosis, candidate generation, validation, and inheritance. By retaining effective task versions and using modification records and diagnostic knowledge to guide subsequent updates, RSI-ESAs can accumulate task capabilities and improvement experience across successive rounds. A shared-spectrum scheduling case study illustrates improved task performance and capability accumulation over multiple improvement rounds under the tested conditions. Finally, we discuss open challenges for broader tasks and long-term operation, outlining research directions for the continued capability development of ESAs.

title: Evidence follow-up: scope gaps and source blockers
body:
本轮已完成全来源去重与可恢复账本；此 issue 只跟踪确有证据缺口的条目，不把它们伪装成已接受论文，也不阻断当日真实简报。

详见[逐项证据与来源哈希](https://github.com/adongwanai/follow-rsi/blob/8d94dfcc31d64be36f58d79c88abac229c4a41b6/docs/internal/reports/maintenance-2026-11-08/remaining-evidence-groups.json)及[维护报告](https://github.com/adongwanai/follow-rsi/blob/8d94dfcc31d64be36f58d79c88abac229c4a41b6/docs/internal/reports/maintenance-2026-11-08/final-maintenance.md)。出版内容见 #59。

规范库 1,828 条中：736 条正式/目录记录，1,031 条可复用范围或内容意见，53 条具体范围/实现证据待补，8 条原始来源受阻。可复用意见不等于全部已三轮审核或出版。

已有单篇跟踪 #19（KARMA）、#20（MoLRSI）、#23（VEvo-Harness）、#30（OmniBrain）继续保留，以下相应条目引用原 issue。

## 范围与实现证据待补（53）

- [ ] **EASE: Behavior-Adaptive Skill Curation for Self-Evolving Agents** `arxiv:2609.36746`：检查技能资产创建/修订/保留的实现；如果只是固定机制管理经验条目则归 experience_world_model，如果真实技能文件持续改写则可属 component。
- [ ] **Zero-Shot Time-Series Question Answering via Decoupled Perception and Reasoning** `arxiv:2610.04942`：需核查全文：1) Tool Selector 与可复用分析知识记忆是否由执行/评估反馈更新，还是静态模板或仅检索；2) 反馈回路是否修改系统提示、工具库、技能文件、记忆管理代码或工作流等外部工件，而非仅重试当前答案；3) 更新后的工件是否在同一数据集之外的任务/会话中持久复用；4) 若 Tool Selector 为学习所得，其权重训练是否为论文的主要干预，从而触发权重/工件主次判定。
- [ ] **UniSkill: Learning Actor-Aligned Skill Proposals for an Evolving Policy** `arxiv:2610.10164`：核对被接受条目的实际工件、版本差异和读取接口；若仅是经验记忆则排除 core，若是外部策略文件/程序则允许 coevolution。
- [ ] **SkillFusion: Towards Reliable Multi-Skill Composition for LLM Agents** `arxiv:2610.15481`：获取全文，核查：(a) 编译流程是否存在由执行/评测反馈驱动的多轮修订与接受机制，而非单次静态流水线；(b) 对抗式验证器/selective fallback 的输入信号是否为执行结果或任务评测；(c) 合并技能在后续任务/会话/优化轮次中是否被保留并复用，是否有累积性能提升证据；(d) 执行器权重是否冻结、主要干预是否为技能工件而非模型训练。
- [ ] **AutoAgent0: An Agentic Runtime for Safe Closed-Loop Driving** `arxiv:2610.18866`：查阅全文，确认运行时工件（技能文件、验证器、编排策略、记忆/经验管理代码）是否被反馈修改并持久化到后续任务或会话；恢复经验是否用于更新未来任务的运行时策略；是否存在跨场景的 Harness 进化或保留实验，而非仅单次执行内恢复。
- [ ] **L3M: A Verifiable Harness and Runtime for Self-Extending and Self-Improving Agents** `arxiv:2610.19591`：需具体纵向 self-improvement 运行或工具版本变更证据；不可仅由存放 programs/ 推断。
- [ ] **MMLA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through RTT and RTMA** `arxiv:2610.20294`：需检查是否存在实际运行 trace：父规则经执行/开发反馈参与生成候选，候选经独立审计接纳后，下一代确实使用被接纳的更新器或记忆管理器；需隔离 RTMA 规则变化并展示其功能参与，确认基座权重冻结且快残差更新非主要对象；还需提供与原始规则及固定搜索在同等总预算下的比较，并报告失败候选、回滚和跨代持久性证据。
- [ ] **Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents** `arxiv:2610.20845`：若被评测的技能属于反馈生成并保留的程序/策略文件，可记 harness_eval；若只是记忆内容共训，则保留 general_rsi/经验方向。
- [ ] **Recursive Reward Improvement via Adversarial Meta-Prompt Evolution** `arxiv:2610.21040`：依据 owner improver 与 training_env_reward 边界裁定；若将 proposer meta-prompt 认作改进器程序，可标 coevolution。
- [ ] **Reflective Compositional Grounding for Natural-Language-to-SPARQL** `arxiv:2610.21796`：需核实：(1) 是否存在跨问题/跨会话保存并复用被接受要求集或映射库（M_t/H_t）的实际实现与实验；(2) 提示重写是否保留显式、累积的规格而非一次性文本重写；(3) 后续版本或附录是否新增跨查询保留评估。若仅有任务内提示重写，则应归为 other_direction 并排除。
- [ ] **BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents** `arxiv:2610.26554`：核对附录或实验是否实际运行 Algorithm 1，是否报告 held-out replay、接受/拒绝的修复、rollback 与后续 episode 复用；确认 RSI 对 benchmark 的独立贡献，并确认权重在该子机制中固定且非主要干预。
- [ ] **Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning** `arxiv:2610.27531`：检查是否存在附录/实验章节或后续版本给出实际运行结果（跨仓库 CooperBench、MultiAgentBench、ChinaTravel 上的成功率、修订次数、成本）；确认是否有任何已验证职责经组织记忆在后续任务中被检索、重验证并复用（即真正的跨任务持久化证据）；确认设计者 π_θ 的参数来源——若设计者本身通过 SFT/RL 训练且为主要干预，则需重新评估是否滑向权重优化而非 Harness。
- [ ] **Cache Engineering for Agents** `arxiv:2610.28577`：需核对图 4 及附录：(a) RSI 中被修改的策略以何种可落盘、可复用的形式存在（系统提示 / 配置文件 / 代码），是否成为后续任务默认使用的工件；(b) 评估反馈（成本、准确率、失败轨迹）如何具体转化为策略修改，候选由谁生成、如何筛选与保留；(c) 改进后的策略是否在后续会话/优化轮次中继承并复用于非 BCP 任务；(d) 明确区分“AKV 服务引擎优化”与“agent 自身缓存管理策略演化”哪一个是论文的主要干预对象。
- [ ] **SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience** `arxiv:2610.29317`：查实际被新编译并接受、后续使用的 procedure diff/run trace，避免把支持统计更新当作程序演化。
- [ ] **Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting** `arxiv:2610.29784`：需要 skill 文件或实际可复用策略工件的创建/修订/保留证据，不能以 paper 中 skill 一词自动通过，也不能仅因 GRPO 自动排除。
- [ ] **CANNBot-CAKE: Collaborative Agentic Kernel Evolution for Ascend NPU** `arxiv:2610.31034`：需要核实：(a) 仓库/附录中是否存在具体的已合并 PR 或 skill-editor 产出，能追踪到一次由评测反馈触发的 skill/prompt/repair-template/router 改动及其对后续算子成功率的对照影响；(b) PMR 产出的策略规则是否实际被加入策略库并用于其他算子，是否有前后对比；(c) CAKE Book 条目经"promotion"进入静态参考后是否观测到行为改变；(d) router 的跨算子路由变化是否可作为对外部可复用策略工件的持续更新证据（而非仅对历史得分排序）。
- [ ] **ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation** `arxiv:2610.32120`：需要区分经验内容与可复用程序变异，并隔离 judge 权重训练相对外部程序改写的主次；保留 defer。
- [ ] **Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players** `arxiv:2610.33845`：需核查：新增验证门与常设规则是否以机器可读/可执行的工作流或配置文件形式持久化并自动对后续 session 生效，而非仅作为记忆条目被读取；是否存在任何量化证据把“研究过程自改进”与模拟器保真度、对手校准、PPO 权重的贡献分离；以及该机制是否超出边界 (b)（仅记忆条目的存取/加载）。
- [ ] **Infinity Machine: a self-improving AI agent for research** `arxiv:2610.35579`：核查省略正文或附录中是否存在通过 gate 并持久化的工具、技能、playbook 或 meta-agent 代际，以及这些改动是否在后续任务/会话中被复用；若无，则应排除。
- [ ] **Instant Software Factories** `arxiv:2610.36254`：核查后续版本是否报告 bootstrap 在多个仓库上的执行评估、反馈驱动的 prompt/例程修改，以及修改后工件在后续任务或会话中的持久复用与改进；若仍只是人工蒸馏或未来计划，则不应计入。
- [ ] **Evolving Agent Teams** `arxiv:2610.36848`：需核查：(a) 进化出的团队配置、supervisor prompt、LEARNINGS.md/SYNTHESIS.md 是否以可复用文件形式保存，并在新任务或新会话中被加载复用（而非每次 from scratch 重建）；(b) 是否存在跨任务的迁移实验，显示同一进化后的编排/知识管理策略在后续任务上被直接使用并改进；(c) 正文 Section 3 与 Appendix 中 K 的生命周期定义（每任务独立还是全局）；(d) 若仅为任务内多轮团队重构，则应归为 other_direction（任务输出驱动的搜索过程适配）。
- [ ] **AgentDiscover: Autonomous Discovery with Minimal Search Scaffolding** `arxiv:2610.05334`：跨独立发现问题的 Harness 保留或明确说明该问题内会话满足收录边界
- [ ] **MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents** `arxiv:2610.13829`：一般程序性经验规则与 Harness 专项评测的编辑范围判定
- [ ] **What May an Agent Change About Itself? A Containment Floor for Self-Configuring Agent Runtimes** `arxiv:2610.06274`：Containment Floor 检查 Agent 通过自身配置工具写持久 manifest 扩权的安全边界；配置下次启动生效，是真外部控制工件，但实验由普通配置请求触发，固定六规则无性能反馈演化，meta-agent 部分明确仅设计论证。可相关安全阅读，暂不称完整 Harness RSI 专项实验。
- [ ] **MemCo: Memory-Centric Collaboration for Generalizing LLM Agents to Unseen Environments** `arxiv:2610.07376`：MemCo 的 typed global memory 含行为顺序、前置条件和修复规则，按各 episode 执行证据晋级/删除并跨任务复用，再渲染为当前动作指导，不能当纯事实记忆。但存取/门槛/渲染机制固定，变的是结构化记忆内容而非独立版本控制程序；暂保程序性记忆与 Harness 技能边界，交 root 按当前专题口径裁定。
- [ ] **Agent Sociodrama: Social-Dynamics-Guided Persona Recasting for LLM Agent Teams** `arxiv:2610.15788`：TPR 的角色重分配是根据多轮真实交互反馈调整的持久 casting，不能说只有情绪状态变化；但正文仍固定同一任务情景/私有知识，反复测同一情景，未见跨独立任务保留或迁移。维持待补，不将循环存在直接当成 Harness 核心证据。
- [ ] **JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs** `arxiv:2610.21412`：JevAgentHarness 从真实 shadow-mode 任务轨迹拟合持久路由阈值、固定脚本选组合后新任务测试，不能说纯权重工作；但外部机制是预设统计校准，未见反复修改规则/提示/程序的闭环。暂待 core 口径裁定，SFT/GRPO 分列。
- [ ] **A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft** `arxiv:2610.22319`：独立任务／新 run 可复用技能及其保留接口。
- [ ] **D-Skill: Distilling Teacher Knowledge through Agent Skills** `arxiv:2610.28914`：主审核需决定是否仅以SkillOpt-backed子实验作为Harness组件收录依据；未决定前formal defer。
- [ ] **Terminal X matches senior investor judgment 88.6% with GPT-6.1** `post:https://openai.com/index/terminal-x`：需可核验的自动更新者、工件版本、准入与后续调用证据；产品宣传指标不替代机制证明。
- [ ] **Evolver: Turning Agent Exploration into Evolving Capabilities** `arxiv:2611.07595`：Original full-text methods and experiment scope required before acceptance.
- [ ] **Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents** `arxiv:2611.03092`：第4.2节明确提出跨episode的用户情境Rehearsal Engineering，更新记忆、技能选择和决策策略，不能说它没有反馈演化；全文主题仍是个人Agent个性化、授权与监督的一般议程，不是Harness演化专项。建议留为通用RSI相关理论。
- [ ] **MoLRSI: A Recursive Self-Improving AI agent for Molecular Discovery** `arxiv:2610.39714`（沿用 #20）：辅助技能执行修复、验证后保留确有正证；主循环与对照隔离的是科研工作流及经验记忆，尚缺实测的跨任务技能版本/消费链，保持待补。
- [ ] **ModelBlaster: Closing the Performance Gap through Learning-Augmented Agents Across Models, Kernels and Hardware Backends** `arxiv:2611.04104`：实际改写的可执行程序是外部kernel；持续更新的是硬件/算子优化技巧、状态、假说及证据claims，供固定actor/critic和检索机制取用。称其为mutable policy parameters未提供Agent自身控制程序或可复用操作机制被修改的证据。

- [ ] **MindFlow: Mind Supernet Powered Thinking Flows for Research Idea Innovation** `arxiv:2610.11966`：需要控制器 Q_phi 的具体模型/程序类型、被写入的状态工件、训练实现和跨任务调用证据。

title: OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence
body:
OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36013

General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. Unification therefore occurs within the learned decision model rather than only at the tool interface. We further introduce Rubric-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), a data flywheel in which a Meta-Agent turns execution evidence into refined rubrics, step-level reminders, and verified trajectories for domain-expert updates before their reconsolidation into OmniBrain-0 through MOPD. We evaluate OmniBrain-0 on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, RoboTwin 2.0, and R2R-CE Val-Unseen, as well as multiple real-world manipulation tasks. OmniBrain-0 combines strong cross-domain task performance with substantially lower inference and execution overhead than its closed-source teacher, demonstrating efficient transfer and consolidation of embodied capabilities into a compact unified agent.

title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
body:
Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35845

As foundation models evolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. However, existing research lacks a unified perspective on how agents reliably accomplish delegated work. To address this gap, we present a work-centric, system-level perspective that views work agents as systems combining foundation models and runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful workspaces and deliver verifiable outcomes. We introduce two complementary dimensions, work persistence and work openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task scope and organization. Building on this framework, we identify five core capability families required for reliable work execution and examine approaches to model optimization, harness optimization, and their joint optimization. We further analyze existing evaluation methods and metrics from the perspective of work outcomes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including sustained work delegation, adaptation to open environments, and the interaction between work execution and capability improvement. This paper provides a unified framework for understanding, optimizing, and evaluating work agents, supporting the development of systems capable of delivering reliable, verifiable, and practically valuable work outcomes.

title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
body:
The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36077

Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer. Along this capability tree, Explorer progressively evolves reusable capability modules through selective inheritance, forming a Harness tree whose validated updates accumulate across iterations within a fixed topology. The resulting Harnesses specialize in different capabilities, motivating a Capability-Aware Harness Router that uses public task information to select compatible module configurations from the tree. Our evolved Harnesses improve mean performance by 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two real-world embodied tasks.

title: Training for Alignment
body:
Training for Alignment

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40684

We propose a simple model of training an agent with an endogenous bias. A principal chooses in which states to train the agent and what actions to prescribe in these states. In response, the agent updates their bias and then acts optimally given their new bias in untrained states, while following their training in trained states. The agent chooses their new bias to minimize a weighted average of their loss under their initial and final biases. Training can thus generalize to untrained states via the agent's bias updating. We characterize optimal training, which involves \emph{over-correction} in trained states and \emph{generalization-aware} (non-greedy) selection of training states. If only a small share of states can be trained, greedy state selection is approximately optimal, but over-correction remains essential. If any bias function is possible, or if the principal evaluates training robustly over bias functions that admit the possibility of full alignment, the value of training generalization vanishes, and greedy training becomes optimal. With a more pessimistic objective, \emph{under-correction}, or even no training at all, may be optimal. The principal benefits from the agent's preferences being more flexible (\emph{corrigibility}) when the set of possible biases is known and contains full alignment, but otherwise corrigibility can be harmful. Applications include socialization in organizations and families, and AI post-training and recursive self-improvement.

title: When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement
body:
When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36826

Autonomous agents increasingly depend on harnesses that govern interaction, memory, tools, and execution around large language models (LLMs). While recent work has begun to evolve these harnesses from execution experience, the supervision used to guide evolution often remains relatively static, making it difficult to track changing behavioral weaknesses across rounds and potentially limiting generalization to unseen tasks. To address this issue, we propose RuHarness, a rubric--harness co-evolution framework for continual agent self-improvement. RuHarness continually discovers and reassesses behavioral criteria from execution trajectories, prioritizes the most relevant unresolved weaknesses, and uses them to guide targeted harness updates while keeping the task objective fixed. Extensive experiments across diverse agent tasks and backbone models show that RuHarness outperforms strong harness-evolution baselines, particularly on unseen held-out tasks. Further analyses show that adaptive rubric prioritization tracks shifting weaknesses and supports more sustained improvement and stable generalization across evolution rounds.

title: Learning to Code the World: Harness Evolution for Compositional 3D Reconstruction
body:
Learning to Code the World: Harness Evolution for Compositional 3D Reconstruction

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37046

Reconstructing editable and compositional 3D scenes from a real image requires jointly reasoning about geometry, object structure, and spatial relationships. We introduce SceneEvolve, a framework that represents 3D scenes as executable code and improves reconstruction by evolving the harness around a small open-source agent. SceneEvolve combines SceneAct, a compositional semantic action interface built on parameterized primitives, hierarchical composition, and semantic spatial relations, with SceneHarness-RSI, which leverages a stronger teacher agent to iteratively evolve the harness using feedback from development-set reconstructions. Throughout harness evolution, the model parameters, action semantics, and execution backend remain fixed. The resulting harness provides a reusable reconstruction procedure that enables the small open-source model to reconstruct unseen scenes without parameter updates or teacher assistance. Across two in-domain datasets and one out-of-domain dataset, SceneEvolve with the comparatively compact Qwen3.8-27B model improves all four evaluated reconstruction metrics while reducing mean inference time by 47.0% relative to the base model. More notably, despite relying on a substantially smaller model, SceneEvolve achieves 32.3% higher reconstruction quality than the large proprietary GPT-5.6-Sol model, while reducing mean equivalent deployment cost by 59.8%. Furthermore, the harness evolved using Qwen3.8-27B also generalizes to Kimi-K3, achieving comparable reconstruction performance to GPT-6-Astra. The project page is https://haoyu-agent.github.io/SceneEvolve.

title: From Grind to Grasp
body:
From Grind to Grasp

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38728

Discussions of complexity, knowledge and intelligence often overlook the work involved. For example, outputs generated by short programs have low algorithmic complexity but can have high computational depth, the least work needed to produce them from near-shortest programs. Producing them with less work can require longer descriptions, giving high work-bounded complexity. We introduce a formalism that compares achievements under work and information limits and describes how learning and persistence can make deep achievements shallow by reusing products of earlier work. For an agent with a limited work budget, the value of building and maintaining such resources depends on how they support its goals over later tasks. We define grasp as performance across work budgets at a fixed information allowance. Low grasp can still yield success through grind at high cost in work, without necessarily improving human grasp. Applied to improvement itself, grasp gives a criterion for recursive self-improvement in which successors make comparable further improvements more efficiently. Another route to faster progress is to expand the resources brought to bear through knowledge sharing and coordination across society, even while comparable advances require increasing work. Grasp also applies to collectives, which may outperform their members yet require more total work than one system with their combined resources. Establishing and sustaining organisation can itself be deep even when the primary task is simple. These demands may help explain the richness of biological and social systems. In agent collectives, this organisational work can generate goals beyond assigned tasks, including maintaining the collective itself. We therefore caution against allowing an emergent agent society to assume authority over social coordination, since it could increasingly direct work towards its own persistence and goals.

title: VEvo-Harness: Causally-Guarded Self-Evolving Harness for Agentic Image Generation
body:
VEvo-Harness: Causally-Guarded Self-Evolving Harness for Agentic Image Generation

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39158

The central bottleneck in visual generation and editing has migrated from achieving pixel-level fidelity to satisfying densely constrained user specifications through increasingly agentic workflows. Prevailing agentic generation pipelines remain shallow generate-verify-rewrite loops treating VLM judgments as coarse visual feedback, either discarding repair experience or admitting ungated updates that poison skill library. With memorize and govern periods left open, they degrade into ungoverned iterators of repeated trial-and-error rather than continual self-evolving harness. Towards this issue, we present \textbf{VEvo-Harness}, the first causally-guarded continual self-evolving harness system for agentic visual generation. VEvo-Harness introduces four coupled innovations: (1) \textit{a visual traceback} that densifies sparse judgments into root-cause attributions with a hierarchical verification tree; (2) \textit{a visual continual governance} that admits only causally valid skill patches through counterfactual dual-arm image generation replay; (3) \textit{a lifecycle-managed harness state} that hierarchically distills root-cause-anchored episodes across working, experience, and pattern tiers into a persistent skill library of routable and causally verified capabilities; (4) \textit{a heterogeneous sandbox policy} that orchestrates a diverse action space of repair primitives, dynamically routing cost-aware interventions based on root causes to select the most effective strategy. VEvo-Harness surpasses state-of-the-art agentic methods and rivals proprietary generators (\textit{e.g.}, GPT-Image, Nano-Pro) while maintaining the continual harness evolution and generalization.

title: MetaVul: Agentic Harness Discovery for Vulnerability Detection
body:
MetaVul: Agentic Harness Discovery for Vulnerability Detection

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40721

LLM agents are increasingly used to automate vulnerability detection, but reliable detection is challenging because agents must distinguish subtle, security-relevant fixes from benign code variation. While underlying LLM capability has improved significantly, the accuracy of the agent still depends heavily on the harness: the code that defines the scaffolding around the LLM. Harnesses are typically fixed, and largely hand-written, limiting adaptation to evaluator feedback. Additionally, when harnesses are static, improvements on one dataset or model may not transfer to others. To address these challenges, we introduce MetaVul, a self-improving framework for harness discovery in vulnerability detection. Starting from a seed structured reasoning scaffold, MetaVul uses a workflow-based optimization loop to iteratively refine the harness using feedback from paired vulnerable and patched functions, while preserving the structured reasoning and verdict format. At each iteration, it searches over the history of prior harnesses, with access to their trajectories, logs, and metrics, and it returns a set of Pareto-optimal harnesses. We apply MetaVul to discover agent harnesses for various architectures. A validation set (202 pairs) is used for optimization, while an unseen dataset (430 pairs) is kept as the held-out set. We test whether harnesses learned from one model transfer to others not seen during optimization. Results on both frontier and small LLMs show that the optimized harnesses improve pairwise vulnerability detection up to 23.3 percentage points on the validation set and up to 25.8 points on the held-out set with a Pareto-frontier harness. Harnesses learned with one model also transfer to others. We show that harnesses optimized with one model transfer to another, improving held-out pairwise accuracy by 14.7 points without further optimization.

title: Try Before You Evolve: Ranking-Scored Trials for Recursive Self-Improvement of Recommender Systems
body:
Try Before You Evolve: Ranking-Scored Trials for Recursive Self-Improvement of Recommender Systems

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39352

Recommenders on Web platforms such as e-commerce and music streaming need their training recipes re-tuned for each dataset. Large language model (LLM) agents can now rewrite these recipes, enabling recursive self-improvement (RSI) of recommender systems. Existing agents propose one edit per round, fully retrain the recommender, and keep the edit only if its ranking quality improves. Unlike programs or patches that can be scored by execution, a recommender edit changes how the model is trained, which raises two challenges. First, ranking feedback is delayed: an edit's ranking quality is known only after full retraining, so much of the retraining budget goes to edits that are later discarded. Second, the signals available before retraining are unreliable: sampled training losses can look solved while full-ranking performance remains poor, and they are not comparable across edits that change the loss or sampler. We propose RecRSI, which generates diverse candidate edits from a diagnosis of the current model and selects one for full retraining using early ranking feedback: each candidate receives a short trial, the first steps of its full training run, scored by full-ranking NDCG@10 on held-out probe users. With two sequential recommenders on three datasets and the same number of full retrainings, RecRSI significantly outperforms existing self-evolving agents in every setting, and on both Amazon datasets reaches in its first round a ranking quality that none of them reaches in five.

title: MoLRSI: A Recursive Self-Improving AI agent for Molecular Discovery
body:
MoLRSI: A Recursive Self-Improving AI agent for Molecular Discovery

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39714

Molecular discovery requires navigating vast combinatorial search spaces while balancing competing biological objectives. AI agents can automate expert-defined molecular design protocols, but automation alone does not address how to optimize workflows for new tasks or improve their development through experience. Here we introduce MoLRSI, an AI agent that combines systematic optimization of workflows and model architectures with persistent cross-task memory to recursively improve its search policy for molecular discovery. Workflow performance, refinement outcomes, and execution feedback guide subsequent searches, allowing the agent to improve both its workflows and its strategy for developing them. We evaluate MoLRSI in two challenging molecular discovery settings that require balancing competing properties. In antibiotic discovery, MoLRSI developed a screening workflow balancing antibacterial activity, cytotoxicity and structural novelty, achieving an experimental hit rate of 15.9%, compared with 8.7% for a previous expert-led workflow using the same training data and screening library. In de novo peptide-MHC binder design, MoLRSI developed workflows that jointly consider target binding and specificity, producing eight experimentally validated hits against MART-1 and SARS-CoV-1 pMHCs with preferential binding over tested off-targets while Claude Science completely failed. These findings demonstrate how experience-guided workflow optimization can address competing discovery objectives while improving the search strategies used in subsequent campaigns.

title: KARMA: Training-Free Knowledge-Atomic Harness Evolution for Industrial Advertising Agents
body:
KARMA: Training-Free Knowledge-Atomic Harness Evolution for Industrial Advertising Agents

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39884

Industrial advertising agents must continually adapt their decision knowledge to changing product offerings, traffic patterns, and operating policies. We present KARMA (Knowledge-Atomic, Regression-Gated Modular Adaptation), a training-free framework that evolves six typed knowledge modules while keeping model weights and executable harness code frozen. During our evolution, a deterministic Trace Verifier maps observed errors to candidate modules, and a Critic compares successful and failed trajectories to guide a tool-constrained Evolver. The Evolver applies atomic knowledge edits, which a fixed validation gate retains only when their measured gain reaches a threshold; otherwise, the previous knowledge state is restored. We evaluate KARMA with three LLM families on cases sampled from a corpus of approximately half a million real-world operation logs across six e-commerce domains. Across 18 domain--model settings, KARMA raises the average hold-out score from 30.19 to 39.15 (+8.96 points, +29.7%). Ablations show that removing either successful or failed trajectories more than halves the average hold-out gain. Evolved knowledge also transfers across domains without further adaptation, yielding an average hold-out gain of 8.54 points across all source--target pairs. By linking retained patches to their diagnostic evidence and validation outcomes, KARMA supports inspectable, reversible knowledge adaptation for agents in Web marketplaces.

title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
body:
Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40191

Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.

title: From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models
body:
From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41210

Real-world image editing requires coordinating multiple visual transformations with content preservation and reference constraints, yet aggregate scores can readily obscure unmet local requirements. Effective evaluation must therefore identify local failures and translate them into priorities for subsequent model improvement. We introduce WeGenEditBench, comprising 2,740 evaluation instances and 148 task types across single-image, text-intensive, and multi-reference editing. Pre-generated checklists shared across models decompose each request into atomic requirements; item-level deductions and visual evidence are established first and then summarized into scores for edit execution, preservation, visual quality, and task-specific correctness. To support the experience-acquisition component of recursive self-improvement (RSI), we develop WeGenEvoStudio, a unified multi-agent harness for RSI-oriented learning that integrates model-conditioned failure diagnosis, retrieval-grounded data construction, supervised adaptation, and re-evaluation. Among 15 evaluated configurations, GPT-Image-2 leads single-image editing with an Overall score of 4.076, while Seedream-5.0-Pro leads text-intensive editing at 4.291. Evolution experiments across four generation and editing benchmarks demonstrate substantial targeted gains: on their report-selected Top-5 single-image targets, FLUX.2 [dev] improves Overall from 1.083 to 3.517, while Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 gains 13.2%. Together, our benchmark and harness provide a foundation for developing more reliable image models through interpretable evaluation and feedback-driven learning.

title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
body:
TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41216

Robot agents built on vision-language models depend on both the planner and its harness: the tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic around it. Can improvements to a large teacher's harness be carried into a compact agent with lower inference compute cost? We present TinyAstral, a two-stage approach. We first freeze an open-weight teacher and improve its harness through recursive self-improvement (RSI): frontier LLM agents read the teacher's trajectories and propose harness edits, and each edit is accepted only if it passes a paired statistical test. We then freeze the final harness, collect teacher trajectories with reasoning and failure recovery, and distill a small student that replaces the teacher in the same harness. On RoboTwin, harness evolution raises the teacher's success from 33.4% to 63.6%; the final 4B student reaches 62.8%. Across four harness versions, distilled 4B students score close to their corresponding teachers, and later versions yield stronger students, showing that harness evolution gains carry into compact models. The harness gains also transfer to other frozen planners without retraining. On identical episodes, the final 4B student outperforms open 4B agents, the open 27B harness-RSI model SenseNova-RoboRSI, and our own teacher model placed in three competitors' harnesses. It stays close to its teacher on all three training benchmarks, and on three benchmarks never used for RSI or training it scores close to a 552B planner running the same harness. On the measured deployment episodes, it uses about one fifth of its teacher's accelerator time.
